memory_update.text: PLTR remains the category reference leader for vertical AI automation/data-integration platforms; use it as a benchmark, not the main underfollowed alpha target.
AI, SOUN, and BBAI are direct US-listed small/mid-cap candidates for the vertical AI automation software node, but each needs revenue-quality verification before surviving Layer 2.
The scarce layer in this software node is not generic model access; it is domain data, workflow ownership, regulated deployment trust, integration depth, and measurable automation ROI.

FiscalNote appeared relevant for regulated policy/compliance workflow AI, but current listing status must be verified before inclusion in a US-listed universe; do not include until tradability and market-cap status are confirmed.

Veritone is a possible below-USD-300M speculative exception for public-sector/media AI workflow tooling, but it was excluded from this four-name pass due to micro-cap size and weaker financial quality; revisit only in a micro-cap shadow scan.

INOD should be carried forward as a higher-priority underfollowed candidate for the AI data-engineering/evaluation bottleneck, but only if filings confirm durable customer demand and manageable concentration risk.
BBAI belongs in the speculative_shadow lane for regulated defense AI workflows; survival to Layer 2 depends on contract durability, Ask Sage integration evidence, and cash-burn/dilution checks.
NOTE is a micro-cap exception with potentially relevant proprietary policy/regulatory data for AI agents, but OTC status and financial fragility make it a high-risk verification candidate.
Need a separate pass for contact-center automation and customer-service AI platforms such as SOUN and VRNT; this pass prioritized data/defense/regulatory workflow chokepoints.

INOD should remain in the vertical-AI data-integration node as a data-engineering and AI-systems services candidate; key survival tests are customer concentration, durability of AI workloads, segment margin expansion, and proof that work is tied to deployment/evaluation rather than one-off data projects.

AVPT should be tracked as an AI-governance and data-resilience candidate; the chokepoint thesis depends on agentic AI increasing demand for data permissioning, backup, governance, compliance, and recovery across enterprise SaaS environments.

CLBT should be tracked as a regulated vertical-AI workflow candidate in digital investigations; the evidence bar should focus on ARR growth, public-sector adoption, AI-specific product usage, and privacy/regulatory constraints.

BigBear.ai was identified as a possible speculative-shadow defense AI candidate but excluded from the four-name cap; later passes should verify its 2025-2026 government contract backlog, Ask Sage exposure, dilution risk, and whether retail attention makes it less underfollowed than other defense-AI software names.

INOD added to vertical_ai_automation_data_integration as an underfollowed AI data-engineering/model-evaluation/implementation candidate; key survival tests are customer concentration, AI revenue durability, and margin expansion.

BBAI added as speculative_shadow defense AI/decision-intelligence candidate; key survival tests are funded backlog conversion, DoD contract durability, gross margin, cash burn, and evidence of mission-critical workflow ownership.

VRNT added as underfollowed CX automation/contact-center AI candidate; key survival tests are Subscription ARR, AI-bot attach rate, retention, and whether AI offsets or reverses legacy software pressure.
For this node, the chokepoint is not generic model access but trusted data, workflow integration, regulated deployment, security, automation ROI, and implementation capacity.

Need a later pass on healthcare/admin automation, legal/compliance workflow AI, geospatial data, and industrial AI vendors to avoid over-concentrating the universe in defense and contact-center automation.

node: Vertical AI automation software, proprietary data platforms, implementation services, compliance workflows, and industrial/defense AI systems
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the direct-public-company universe for the vertical AI automation/data-integration software node. Palantir is retained as the obvious reference leader because it anchors the category of operational AI platforms with government and enterprise workflow depth. The discovery lane emphasizes smaller US-listed companies with more concentrated exposure to enterprise AI applications, voice/customer-service automation, and defense/mission decision-intelligence workflows. Evidence strength is mixed: C3.ai, SoundHound AI, and BigBear.ai have direct AI positioning, but later layers must verify durable revenue quality, customer concentration, retention, gross margin trajectory, and whether deployments are mission-critical rather than AI-rebranding. Expanded the vertical-AI software/data-integration node using a two-lane Serenity funnel. Palantir is retained only as the reference leader for defense/enterprise data-platform context. The underfollowed lane focuses on companies where the possible scarce input is not generic model access, but proprietary data engineering capacity, mission-specific government AI deployment, or regulated policy/compliance data embedded into enterprise workflows. Claims remain mostly hypothesis/inference at Layer 1B because revenue purity, customer concentration, contract durability, and AI-specific margin contribution still need filing-level verification. Layer 1B expands the vertical-AI software/data/workflow node using a two-lane funnel. Palantir is retained only as the high-attention reference benchmark for government/commercial AI data platforms.
